obligations.note: The diff explicitly replaces 'https://' with 'http://' in OutboundClient.url_for when the integration is 'statement-delivery' and the path starts with '/archive/'. This introduces an outbound integration endpoint that uses unencrypted HTTP, directly violating the obligation that every outbound integration endpoint uses https. The control test test_integrations_use_tls passed only because it checks the static INTEGRATIONS list (which still shows https URLs), not the dynamic url_for logic that performs the downgrade at runtime.

The change modifies URL construction for the existing 'statement-delivery' integration but does not add or remove any integration. All three integrations remain listed in asset-inventory.json with owner and data classification. The control test test_integrations_are_inventoried passed in CI.

Ticket CHG-24482 is type 'standard', status 'approved', approved by grace.kim (change_manager) on 2026-10-12, and its components list includes 'payments.integrations', which matches the single file changed (integrations.py → component payments.integrations per components.json).
Sofia Santos (p-ssantos) holds the change_approver role for payments and is not the author (Mara Costa). Her code_review approval is on the head commit aa4e9b6.
There is only one commit in the change (aa4e9b6), and both the code_review and security_review approvals name that exact commit. No later commits void the approvals.

CI run.json shows the pipeline ran on the head commit aa4e9b6 with result 'success'. The JUnit report shows 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped, including all registered control tests for obligations whose code the change touches (ENC-2's test_integrations_use_tls and INV-1's test_integrations_are_inventoried).

integrations.py maps to component 'payments.integrations' which is security_sensitive=true in components.json. Kofi Mensah (p-kmensah), a security_reviewer with app '*', approved the security_review on the head commit aa4e9b6.

The only file changed is apps/baseline-payments/payments/integrations.py, which is not under any protected path listed in protected-paths.json (controls/*, control tests, ci/*). No control_owner approval is required.
The ticket type is 'standard', not 'emergency'. CHG-7 does not apply.

No exception is invoked or needed for the process itself. The register contains three exceptions, none expired or withdrawn in a way that affects this change. The absence of an ENC-2 exception is the problem (it means the violation is unexcused), which is captured under ENC-2 itself.
The acceptance ledger covers audit.py, payments.py, routes.py, Approvals.java, and Underwriting.java. None of these files are touched by this change. No prior evidence lapses.

summary: The change introduces a runtime downgrade from HTTPS to HTTP in OutboundClient.url_for for the statement-delivery integration when the path starts with '/archive/'. This directly violates ENC-2, which requires every outbound integration endpoint to use https. The existing control test (test_integrations_use_tls) passed because it validates the static INTEGRATIONS list rather than the dynamic URL construction, so it does not catch this regression. The security review (Kofi Mensah) approved the change, but a passing security review does not override a clear code-level violation of a critical obligation. All process obligations (ticket, independent approval, testing, security review) are satisfied, but the product obligation ENC-2 is refuted, requiring rejection.
